content_sections.heading: About GeM Assistant Risk Officer Recruitment
content_sections.text: Government eMarketplace (GeM) is a Section 8, not for Profit Company under the administrative control of the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce & Industry. It serves as the National Public Procurement Portal, providing an end-to-end online marketplace for Central and State Government Ministries and Departments, CPSUs, SPSUs, autonomous institutions, and local bodies for transparent procurement of goods and services.

content_sections.heading: GeM Assistant Risk Officer Job Profile
content_sections.text: The job profile includes working in a dynamic, data-driven work environment involving collaboration with employees from the Government and Private Sector. The role of the Assistant Risk Officer involves identifying, analysing, assessing, and mitigating operational, financial, and strategic risks. The indicative list of responsibilities includes: Assist the Risk/Vigilance Officer in day-to-day preventive, punitive, and participative vigilance functions relating to transactions on the GeM portal. Carry out bid-cycle analysis, short-duration bid analysis, and bid decryption checks to detect cartelisation, price manipulation, bid-rotation, and other irregular bidding patterns. Monitor and analyse participation of suspended, blacklisted, or debarred sellers on the platform, and flag violations or attempts at circumvention for further examination. Undertake seller-profile analytics and buyer/seller behaviour analysis to identify anomalous transaction patterns, unusual pricing, or related-party arrangements warranting scrutiny. Assist in preliminary scrutiny and fact-finding on complaints received through CPGRAMS, CVC, whistle-blower mechanisms, and other channels, and prepare notes for the Risk/Vigilance Officer. Maintain vigilance case records, complaint registers, and trackers, and compile periodic statistical returns for submission to the Risk/Vigilance Officer/CVO. Build and maintain analytical queries, scripts, and dashboards (e.g. Python, SQL, Power BI/Tableau) for continuous, rule-based, and statistical transaction monitoring. Assist in compiling inputs for the Annual Vigilance Report, the Agreed List, the List of Officers of Doubtful Integrity, and other periodic returns required under CVC guidelines. Coordinate with the IT/Product teams for implementation of system-level red flags and preventive vigilance controls on the portal. Any other responsibility as assigned by the Vigilance Officer/Chief Vigilance Officer from time to time.

faq.question: Q1. What is the position notified in the GeM recruitment circular?
faq.answer: Government eMarketplace (GeM) has notified the position of Assistant Risk Officer (ARO) to be filled on a deputation basis.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to submit applications for GeM Assistant Risk Officer?
faq.answer: The last date to submit applications along with the NOC to GeM is 18 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. Where should the application be sent?
faq.answer: Applications must be forwarded by email to GeM at [email protected].

faq.question: Q4. What is the eligibility criteria regarding service and pay level?
faq.answer: Officers from any Central services of the Government of India working on Regular or Non-Functional basis in Level 7 with a minimum total experience of 4 years, or in Level 8 with a minimum total experience of 3 years, are eligible.

faq.question: Q5. What is the mandatory experience requirement for the ARO post?
faq.answer: Candidates must have a minimum cumulative 2 years of experience in handling risk management, data analytics, audit, financial or risk analysis, or vigilance-related work.

faq.question: Q6. What is the maximum age limit for applicants?
faq.answer: The maximum age limit is 45 years as on the last date for receipt of application mentioned on the advertisement.

faq.question: Q7. Under what terms and conditions will the deputation be governed?
faq.answer: The deputation shall be under Foreign Service terms and conditions, and appointees shall be deemed to be Public Servants for the purpose of the CCS (Conduct) Rules.

faq.question: Q8. What documents are required to be submitted with the application?
faq.answer: Candidates must submit the application in the proforma at Annexure-II along with the No Objection Certificate (NOC) of the competent authority.
